decisions.reason: Although it is less prominently featured than newer laser systems, it still fits the firm's laser portfolio and the cost of keeping this niche workstation available is likely low relative to the option value of serving smaller or manual-marking applications.
A high-resolution thermal inkjet printer matches the firm's core multi-technology strategy and, since it kept its own page across both years, the evidence does not yet justify abandoning it.

The piezo inkjet printer supports the firm's promise to match marking technology to application, and as a large expanding firm with strong R&D it is likely to keep this option open while market learning continues.
As a 2024 flagship product aligned with digitalized identification and traceability, this is a strategic commitment rather than a candidate for near-term withdrawal.
The compact laser marking cabin is newly launched and closely related to the firm's laser direction, so real-options logic favors retaining it until more demand information is revealed.

Despite being more specialized, the lubricant printing system has external validation from an industry award and should be kept as a promising option while the firm tests the depth of demand in sheet-metal applications.
